Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman with 3 days of progressively worsening headache (right periorbital predominance, constant with fluctuating intensity, 8/10) associated with photophobia and brief “shooting lights,” nausea without vomiting; assessment favored migraine-type headache. Plan included stronger analgesia (prescription offered; exact drug not specified), guidance on ibuprofen dosing, headache diary, follow-up in 1–2 weeks, and return precautions.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache for ~3 days, worsening.
- Location/character: Generalized but mainly around right eye; dull baseline with intermittent sharper pains.
- Severity: 8/10.
- Onset/progression: Gradual onset at work on day 1; worse by end of day; more severe next morning; overall worsening over 3 days.
- Course: Present all the time with fluctuations in intensity.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Tried ibuprofen “a few” tablets over the last two days (three per day); not helpful (previously effective for prior headaches).
  - Patient reduced computer screen brightness; still difficult to focus.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Photophobia; “weird shooting lights” at onset.
  - Nausea without vomiting.
  - Difficulty concentrating; required time off work.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No loss of vision; no blurry vision reported.
  - No speech difficulty.
  - No limb weakness.
  - No recent head injury.
  - No fever; no rash.
  - Neck pain/stiffness: patient first said “Yeah,” then “No” (conflict noted).
- Context:
  - Works in IT with extensive screen use; wears glasses since age 5; no recent eye exam.
  - Mild recent work stress due to new project.
  - Concerned about possibility of migraine given family history.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- No prior diagnosis of migraine.
- Medications:
  - No regular medications reported.
  - Ibuprofen self-treatment for this headache: three tablets/day for last two days (tablet strength not documented); ineffective.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies reported.

Social History:
- Lives with three housemates (total four people).
- Occupation: IT; heavy computer use.
- Tobacco: “Socially” smokes.
- Alcohol: Drinks socially.
- Stress: Some increased stress with new project; not out of the ordinary.

Family History:
- Mother: Migraines, often severe and triggered around seasonal changes.
- Sister: Migraines, infrequent.

Physical Examination:
- (Not documented)

Investigations:
- None documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute worsening headache, probable migraine-type headache.
  - Assessment: Gradual onset; right periorbital predominance; photophobia; positive visual phenomena (“shooting lights”); nausea without vomiting; family history of migraine; no focal neurological symptoms reported; no fever; no rash. Neck stiffness history conflicting (see Quality checks).
  - Plan:
    - Provide stronger analgesia; prescription to be provided today—specific medication not documented. Options discussed: naproxen; and adding paracetamol or codeine.
    - Counsel on correct ibuprofen dosing: up to two tablets, three times daily (tablet strength not documented).
    - Maintain a headache diary to identify triggers.
    - Follow-up in 1–2 weeks; sooner if symptoms worsen or do not improve.
    - Return/urgent precautions: worsening headache, visual problems, weakness in arms/legs, or feeling unwell—call or return sooner.
    - Consider prophylactic therapy if headaches become frequent (to be discussed at follow-up).

- Issue 2: Visual symptoms and photophobia associated with headache.
  - Plan:
    - Continue minimizing bright light/screen brightness as needed.
    - Consider repeat eye test if eyes feel strained (no recent eye exam).

- Issue 3: Work impact due to headache.
  - Plan:
    - Patient already took time off; no additional work accommodations documented.

General plan items:
- None beyond above.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals; full neurological exam (including cranial nerves, fundoscopy), and general physical exam.
  - Pregnancy status and contraception use (clinician asked about “the pill,” no answer documented).
  - Detailed medication reconciliation (strengths, routes, frequencies); exact drug prescribed today not specified.
  - Quantification of tobacco/alcohol use.
  - Red flag screening incomplete for thunderclap onset, exertional onset, positional change, recent infection, immunosuppression, or anticoagulant use.
  - Recent eye exam status noted as absent; no visual acuity documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Neck pain/stiffness: patient first answered “Yeah,” then “No” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor disfluencies and one ambiguous statement regarding which medication was prescribed (“I can give you a prescription for that today”).
